doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: First job at 14: 'Perdido' in B flat
summary: At 14 he was called to a local party house band, handed 'Perdido' in B flat, and transposed from a C fake book.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Sort of anticipated a question I had about that and that was especially in the rock & roll or the jazz is playing the trumpet parts, or playing along with it, was there a point where you got a sense of also hearing the bass notes and figuring out okay this is in mostly this key that’s why these trumpet parts sort of make sense?

Yeah. My first job was when I was 14. Okay? With older musicians. Because I lived about 400 yards from an American Legion — no it wasn’t an American Legion — it was like one of those little party houses. Not a big one, just a little one. And they would have weddings in there and you know the Italian club would meet there and you know things like that. So one night about 9:00 the phone rings and some guy is talking to my dad and he goes, “Absolutely not.” I’m going what’s going on, what’s going on? He says, “No, my son’s not coming out at 9:00 and play with your band. I know you heard he plays pretty well but well okay, I’m coming over there with him.” So he took me over to this place and you know what? My neighbor had given me a fake book. See I did that after school too. I learned some tunes. I didn’t really know the chord changes at all really. So the very first thing I heard from the band leader, “Oh thanks for coming. ‘Perdido’ in B flat.” That was all I had.
Did you have a B flat fake book?
No, no I had a C.
So you had a concert fake book, did you read?
I transposed it. So then I had to play off the staff. And my band director of course in high school, okay, he was great.
